questions.text: With typical parts the battery lasts about 16 months on alkaline AAA. If every part sits at its worst datasheet limit in a warm (50 C) box, it drops to about 11-13 months. How should we handle that?
options: Keep the design, and measure the sleep current on the first 3 boards before building more (recommended: most worst-case figures are upper bounds or estimates; pass if it is 16.7 uA or less)
Check Wi-Fi every 90 minutes instead of 60 (14.4 months even in the worst case; remote changes take up to 90 minutes)
Keep 60 minutes and accept that a worst-case unit lasts about 11-13 months
questions.why: conflicts.md C20. The worst case adds the maximum leakage of every part at 50 C: the Wi-Fi module, the large capacitor and the protection transistor.

questions.text: The relay maker rates the contacts for 5 A on heaters but publishes no figure for the switch-on surge of valve motors. How do we confirm it?
options: Bench test on the first boards: switch a real valve head or zone valve 1,000 times and check the contacts (recommended)
Ask the relay maker for the motor-load rating before ordering boards (may take weeks)
Accept the risk for the prototypes
questions.why: Requirement R6. Thermal heads draw a short surge when cold; the datasheet only covers resistive loads and one UL motor rating.
